intro.en: Me, te, le for whose body or belongings something happens to, and for things other people do for you.

cortarse el pelo.en: to have one's hair cut; to cut one's hair

titulo.en: Whose is it? The pronoun says so

texto.en:
English uses my, your, his. With the body, clothes and belongings, Spanish prefers **me, te, le** plus the article.

- **Le** robaron **el** coche. (his car)
- **Me** han manchado **la** camisa. (my shirt)
- **Te** duele **la** muela. (your tooth)

Accidents use **se me**, **se te**, **se le**: **se me ha roto** el móvil; **se le ha perdido** la cartera.

Services work the same way. Spanish does not say I have had my hair cut. It simply says **me he cortado el pelo**, even when the hairdresser did it. Likewise: **me han arreglado** el grifo; **me sacaron** una muela; **me revisaron** el coche.

An offer: **¿Te hago** un café**?** **¿Te llevo** la maleta**?**

frases.en: What a change! Have you had your hair cut?

frases.es: Sí, y me lo he teñido. Fui a la peluquería esta mañana.
frases.en: Yes, and I've had it dyed. I went to the hairdresser's this morning.

frases.es: Yo he estado en casa con el fontanero. Se nos ha roto un grifo.
frases.en: I've been at home with the plumber. One of our taps has broken.
Has he fixed it for you yet?

frases.es: Sí. Y a mi hermano le robaron la bici anoche.
frases.en: Yes. And my brother had his bike stolen last night.
What a day! Shall I make you a coffee?

Le.en: Le shows whose car it was.

Su.en: Spanish uses le and the article.

Lo.en: Lo would be the thing stolen.

me.en: It happened to me: se me.

mi.en: The pronoun is me, with the article.

pregunta.en: «Me he cortado el pelo.» Who probably cut it?

A hairdresser.en: Spanish says it this way even when someone else does it.

pregunta.en: Complete: my shirt has been stained.

la.en: With me, Spanish uses the article.

mi.en: Me already says whose shirt it is.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about services you have had done lately and things that have been done to you: haircut, repairs, a theft.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Tell aloud about a time when something was stolen from you or broke.
